name: Kingdom of Yugoslavia

areaKm2.note: League of Nations Statistical Year-Book 1939/40, Table 2: Yugoslavia 248 thousand km2 (mid, high). world_1938 Yugoslavia polygon = 242,875 km2 computed by the pipeline (low). The post-1947 state (255,800 km2, CIA World Factbook 1990) adds Istria and Zadar and is not used.

population.note: League of Nations Year-Book 1939/40, Table 2: estimate xii.1938 = 15,630k (low), census 1931 = 13,934k. COW NMC v7 tpop 1940 = 15,811k grown one year at the 1931-38 rate of the League figures ((15,630/13,934)^(1/7) = 1.65% a year) = 16,070k (mid). OWID (https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/population.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true) Yugoslavia 1940 = 16.30M (high).

urbanization.note: HYDE 3.5 via OWID, present-day republics 1940: Bosnia 10.9%, Slovenia 15.9%, Croatia 17.8%, North Macedonia 18.4% (Serbia and Montenegro not in the series); range spans the republics, mid near the population-weighted value. COW upop/tpop 1940 = 774/15,811 = 0.05 counts cities over 100,000 only. Three-quarters of the workforce was in agriculture (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Yugoslavia).

activePersonnel.note: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia: the Yugoslav Army was about 1,200,000 in total as the German invasion began (high; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Yugoslav_Army: the strength at full mobilisation, of whom only ~50% had joined their units); infobox (Tomasevich) 700,000 plus 400,000 ill-prepared. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Yugoslav_Army: mobilised strength 600,000 on 20 March 1941 (low). Mid 900,000 = the 700,000 prepared plus half of the ill-prepared. Includes the air force (1,875 officers + 29,527 men) and navy (611 officers + 8,562 men in 1939, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Yugoslav_Navy). Snapshot date 6 April 1941.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Reservists called up on 3 April 1941 who had not reached their units when the invasion began (about half the recruits, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Yugoslav_Army), plus older classes; the 1.2M full-mobilisation figure bounds the sum.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Everything outside the P roles: ~4,000 guns, 2,300 mortars and 940 AA guns (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia), engineers, signals, the horse trains of an army reliant on animal transport, frontier fortress artillery, air force ~31,000 and navy ~9,000.

mobilizationRatio.note: Mobilised 600,000 (20 March 1941) to ~1,200,000 at full mobilisation (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Yugoslav_Army) of ~16M = 0.04-0.075; mid 0.07 and high 0.08 cover the full plan with the remaining reserve classes.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess. Fully mobilised 28 infantry divisions and 35 independent regiments (16 frontier, 19 combined detachments of 1-3 regiments) (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia); the mobilisation plan gave infantry divisions of about 25,000 men (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Yugoslav_Army), roughly half of them rifle infantry = ~350,000, plus ~100,000 in the independent regiments at full strength; units were filled to 70-90% and only ~11 divisions were in position (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: largely First World War weapons from several countries, some modern Czech equipment, 1,600 modern 81 mm mortars; spare parts and maintenance lacking (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia).

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: conscript army with reservists still arriving; 400,000 of the mobilised men rated ill-prepared (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia infobox).

count.note: Educated guess. Mounted strength of the three cavalry divisions, each with two motorised infantry battalions (six in all, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: horse cavalry with carbines and machine guns.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: regular cavalry cadre.

count.note: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia: two tank battalions with 110 tanks (54 modern Renault R35, the rest Renault FT of First World War origin) (low) plus an independent company of 8 Czech T-32 tank destroyers (mid 118); infobox high 200 (Zajac).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: only 50 tanks could engage German tanks on equal terms (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia).

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: tank battalion formed only in the late 1930s (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Yugoslav_Army).

count.note: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia: about 4,000 artillery pieces (high), including 812 Czech 37 mm and 47 mm AT guns; without the AT guns ~3,188 (low), mid 3,200. Twenty-four 220 mm and 305 mm pieces included; 2,300 mortars not counted.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: many guns aged and horse-drawn, ~1,700 relatively modern (incl. the AT guns); six motorised artillery regiments (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia).

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: regular gunner cadre, reservist crews.

count.note: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia: operational 73 Bf 109E, 47 Hurricane I, 30 Fury II, 11 IK-3, 10 IK-2 and 1 R 313 = 172 (mid); with 2 Potez 63 and a captured Bf 110 = 175 (high); infobox: 107 modern fighters (low, Shores).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Bf 109E, Hurricane and IK-3 equal to their opponents; Fury II biplanes obsolete.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: ~2,000 pilots (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia); few hours on the new types; airfields hit on the first day.

count.note: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia: 69 Do 17K, 61 Blenheim I and 40 SM.79K bombers = 170 (mid; infobox 103 modern bombers, low). High adds 130 Breguet 19 and Potez 25 army reconnaissance light bombers and 27 naval Do 22K and SIM-XIV floatplanes (327).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: Do 17K and Blenheim modern, Breguet 19 and Potez 25 obsolete.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: 22 bomber squadrons (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia).

count.note: AA guns at 4 per battery. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia: 940 AA guns (mid 235 batteries), of which 360 were 15 mm and 20 mm; the 580 heavier guns alone = 145 batteries (low).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: mixed Czech and Italian models without common spares (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia).

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: Belgrade defences failed to stop the 6 April raid.

count.note: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Yugoslav_Navy: flotilla leader Dubrovnik and three Beograd-class destroyers = 4 (mid; Ljubljana in dry dock, low 3). High adds the old training cruiser Dalmacija.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: Dubrovnik (1931) and the Beograd class were modern 1930s destroyers.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: the British rated the commander-in-chief as having little technical knowledge (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Yugoslav_Navy); the fleet was captured almost intact.

count.note: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Yugoslav_Navy: 8 Orjen-class and 2 Uskok-class MTBs (low 10); plus 6 Galeb-class and 5 Malinska-class minelayers and 6 250t-class torpedo boats (mid 27); high adds the 4 Danube river monitors (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: Orjen-class MTBs modern; minelayers and 250t boats of First World War origin.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: as ships_major.

count.note: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Yugoslav_Navy: four submarines, of which only the two French-built boats were fully combat-ready (low 2).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: 1920s British and French boats.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: as ships_major.

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: mobilisation delayed to 3 April, only ~11 divisions in position, a cordon along the whole frontier; the 6 April bombing of Belgrade cut communications between the high command and the field forces (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia); 150 of 167 generals were Serbs, and the 1937 manoeuvres exposed an incompetent General Staff (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Yugoslav_Army).

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.25 (divided). Evidence: resistance collapsed largely because many non-Serbs, Croats in particular, would not fight (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Yugoslav_Army); ethnic German and Hungarian conscripts were released by the Germans after capture (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia).

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.25-0.5. Evidence: Serbian units motivated after the 27 March coup, others not; 254,000-345,000 captured by the Germans in 11 days (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia).

weapons.note: Anchor: 7 (1905) toward 8 (1943). Evidence: First World War rifles and machine guns with some modern Czech equipment, 1,600 modern 81 mm mortars, 812 37 mm and 47 mm AT guns (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia).

armor.note: Anchor: between 7 and 8. Evidence: 54 Renault R35 (cast armour, 37 mm gun), the rest Renault FT.

ships.note: Anchor: 7 toward 8. Evidence: modern destroyers Dubrovnik and Beograd class, Orjen-class MTBs (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Yugoslav_Navy); no cruisers of value.

fortification.note: Anchor: 7 toward 8. Evidence: 16 regiments in frontier fortifications (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia); no continuous concrete line comparable to the Czechoslovak or Maginot works.

logistics.note: Anchor: 7 (railways). Evidence: heavily reliant on animal-powered transport; 1,000 US trucks imported in the months before the invasion (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia).

communications.note: Anchor: 7 (telephone and telegraph). Evidence: the bombing of Belgrade destroyed nearly all means of communication with the field forces (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia).

isr.note: Anchor: 7 toward 8. Evidence: seven reconnaissance groups with 130 Breguet 19 and Potez 25 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia); no radar.

air.note: Anchor: 8 (1943). Evidence: Bf 109E, Hurricane I, IK-3, Do 17K and Blenheim I, most aircraft modern types (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia).

cyber.note: No military computer networks before ~1990 (cyber anchor 9 = 1990 networks).

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (OWID CSV) Yugoslavia: 1939 = 2,072 (mid, high), 1938 = 1,991 (low), 2011 int$. No 1940-41 value.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Global Military Spending Dataset via OWID, Yugoslavia: 1940 = 7.43% (low, last peacetime; 1939 6.85%), 1941 = 15.0% (mid, high: at war). COW milex 1940 = 121,456 thousand current US$.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Industry and mining share of output. Three-quarters of the workforce was in agriculture and more than half of industrial workers were seasonal worker-peasants (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Yugoslavia).

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - agricultural share of employment (s = 1 assumed: Yugoslavia exported grain and livestock in the 1930s). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Yugoslavia: three-quarters of the workforce in agriculture -> 1 - 0.75 = 0.25; mostly subsistence peasants, poor in the south.

annualCohort.note: Educated guess. Men reaching military age (21) per year: the 1920 birth cohort of ~12M people at ~35 births per 1,000 = ~420,000, half male, ~65% survival.

aircraft_strike.note: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia: about 40 Do 17K and some 40 Blenheim I licence-built in Yugoslavia, mostly 1939-41: ~40 a year.

aircraft_fighter.note: Educated guess. Hurricanes under licence and IK-3 fighters under construction at the invasion (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia); IK-3 output was a dozen.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Roads of all classes, few paved; the 1987 network of 120,747 km (CIA World Factbook 1990, https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/14/pg14.txt) was mostly built after 1945.

railKm.note: Educated guess. Standard and narrow-gauge lines of the Yugoslav State Railways; the 1987 network was 9,270 km (CIA World Factbook 1990) after post-war additions and closures.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Split, Sibenik, Susak, Dubrovnik (Gruz) and the Bay of Kotor naval base; Belgrade on the Danube.

merchantTonnage.note: GRT to DWT x 1.5 (low x 1.3, high x 1.6). League of Nations Year-Book 1939/40 Table 113 (https://www.istmat.org/files/uploads/49915/09_strany_mira_-_transport_torgovlya_platyozhnyy_balans.pdf): Yugoslavia 387k GRT in June 1938.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Animal-powered trains from the railheads; ~1,000 trucks in all (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia).

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. National stock of horses (and oxen used for transport) in a peasant economy of 16M; the army relied on requisitioned animals.

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row for the Dinaric mountains, reduced to 1.1 because much of the population did not support the defence (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Yugoslav_Army) and the Danube plain in the north is open; low 1.0.

notes: Snapshot date 6 April 1941, the first day of the Axis invasion, with mobilisation ordered on 3 April and incomplete. Active personnel spans the 600,000 mobilised on 20 March to the 1.2M of full mobilisation (mid 900,000). Equipment from the Invasion of Yugoslavia article (Tomasevich, Zajac, Shores, Cull and Malizia) and the Royal Yugoslav Navy article (Vego, Niehorster). Weakest values: the P-role split, support personnel, roads, railway length and animals (educated guesses; no interwar railway or road total was fetched). Ship convention per SOURCES.md: destroyers ships_major; MTBs, minelayers, torpedo boats and river monitors ships_minor.
